ROOT_CAUSE: The recovery itself was the risk, not a bug in it. runtime.py answered SAFE_STOP unknown_page by pressing the system Back key immediately and then re-observing, up to max_unknown_page_backs times per run. That is the right call for an ordinary unrecognised screen and it was written for exactly that case (2026-09-14: a Hero Journey mission card in a skin no template matched). A live battle is a different situation with the same symptom: measured on the one recorded battle frame (dataset/raw/control_panel/probe/live_page_20260915_151446.png, 2026-09-15 15:14:46) the page model answers Page.UNKNOWN at confidence 0.0 -- it genuinely cannot name a battle screen -- so the ordinary recovery would press Back into a fight whose response to Back has never been measured. Separability was checked before anything was changed, and it is absent: of the recorded frames that could plausibly be battle or transition, the battle frame is UNKNOWN and every Hero Journey frame resolves to a known page (MAP, INTEL, POPUP, MARCH, EXPLORATION), so there is no threshold or detail field that separates 'battle' from 'ordinary unknown' in the existing corpus. The order anticipated exactly this and named the alternative, so the fix is run-scoped context rather than a new classifier.
PATCH_SUMMARY: Run-scoped, no new architecture. LiveRuntime gained FIGHT_STARTING_VERIFIERS = {"INTEL_HERO_DISPATCHED"} and a max_battle_reobservations bound (3, a sibling of the existing max_unknown_page_backs). After a step whose verifier passes and whose skill's verifier is in that set, _fight_resolving is set; while it is set, an unknown_page STOP waits and re-observes instead of pressing Back, bounded by the same shape as the Back loop, and reports unknown_page unchanged if the screen never resolves. The flag is cleared at the start of every run and as soon as any known page is observed, so it cannot outlive the fight it was armed for. The arming condition reads the verifier from the skill registry rather than a hand-written skill list, which is what keeps the set narrow: INTEL_HERO_DISPATCHED is the only such verifier in the registry today.
TEST_RESULT: tests/test_battle_unknown_recovery.py: 8 passed. The acceptance asks for a negative control, so the tests are built as pairs. Negative control (RuleBrain, nothing dispatched): an ordinary unknown screen still presses Back, and still recovers when Back reaches a known page -- asserted first, because the risk of this change is weakening the recovery it was meant to leave alone. Armed path (scripted brain: dispatch on MARCH, honest stop on UNKNOWN): after a verified dispatch no Back is pressed at all; the wait is bounded and stops early when the screen resolves; the stop reason is still reported as unknown_page so recovery does not hide the root cause; the flag is cleared at the start of a new run. Two further tests pin the arming rule to the registry: INTEL_HERO_DISPATCH must carry the verifier, and the set must stay small because each addition weakens the ordinary recovery.
REPLAY_RESULT: tools/cq_battle_separability.py measured every candidate frame through the production observe path first. Battle frame -> Page.UNKNOWN confidence 0.0. hero_live6 step003 before -> MAP 0.99; step003/005 after -> INTEL 0.99/0.98; step004 after -> POPUP 0.99 (EXPLORATION_REWARD); hero_live5 step001 after -> MARCH 0.99; hero_live3 step001 after -> EXPLORATION 0.99; HOME control -> HOME 0.98. Conclusion recorded rather than worked around: the recorded corpus contains exactly one battle frame and no ordinary-unknown frame to contrast it with, so 'battle' is not separable from 'unknown' with the templates that exist, and a detector would have had to be invented. Template registration is also outside this order's file scope, which independently rules out that route.
LIVE_DETAIL: No live attempt, by design and by the order's own live_plan: 'only observe when a battle naturally occurs; do not initiate additional battles to manufacture the state'. No battle occurred during this round. The behaviour change is therefore verified by replay of the recorded battle frame plus deterministic tests, and NOT by a live battle - which is the honest status and is recorded as the remaining gap.

BEFORE: Any unknown screen, including a live battle, was answered by pressing the system Back key immediately, once or twice per run.
AFTER: An unknown screen that follows a verified fight dispatch is waited out with bounded re-observation and no Back press; every other unknown screen is handled exactly as before, which the negative-control tests assert.
VERIFIER_RESULT: not applicable - no live step was taken; the deterministic tests and the replay are the evidence
REMAINING_ISSUE: The armed branch has never been exercised against a real battle. The order forbids manufacturing one, so the honest status is: branch verified by test and by replay of the one recorded battle frame, unverified live. The first natural battle after this change is the moment to confirm it, and the runtime's own episode record will show it (screenshots suffixed battle_wait, no PRESS_BACK step).

The armed set contains one verifier because the registry has one. DISPATCH_INTEL_BEAST and DISPATCH_BEAST carry NO verifier at all (no verifier= argument in skills.py), so a Beast fight dispatch cannot arm anything and a Beast battle screen would still be Backed out of. That is a data gap, not an oversight: widening the set needs frames of a Beast battle screen, which do not exist yet.

Acceptance asked for 'negative control passes' and that is met for the two paths that exist. It would be stronger with a frame of an ordinary unknown screen that is NOT a battle -- the corpus has none, because every unrecognised screen in it turned out to be a skin or an animation the templates later covered.
